flags: Gran Tierra signed a share sale agreement to sell its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses to Maurel & Prom Andina for total consideration of $1.33 billion, including assumed debt. Closing is still subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business section and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Gran Tierra is an oil and gas exploration and production company. It sells oil, natural gas and NGLs produced from assets in Colombia, Canada and Ecuador.
quotes: is a company focused on oil and gas exploration and production, with assets in Colombia, Canada and Ecuador

business_model.claim: In 2025 revenue was concentrated in Colombia at 70%, with Canada at 19% and Ecuador at 11%. Canada and Ecuador have grown their shares since 2024.
quotes: 19% of our revenue was generated in Canada (2024 - 3%; 2023 - nil)

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors. Named customers are not in the evidence.
business_model.claim: Realized prices are set by contracts with purchasers. They are based on international benchmark prices less deductions for quality differentials and transportation.
quotes: are established by contracts with purchasers and include the deductions for quality differentials and transportation

business_model.basis: The balance is stated. The link to a prepayment arrangement is inferred.

quotes: Customer advance (Note 7)

business_model.basis: Stated in the MD&A and press release tables. The segment label is inferred.
business_model.claim: The MD&A reports results and operating netback by country: Colombia, Ecuador and Canada. For the nine months to Sep. 30, 2026, operating netback was 205,734 in Colombia, 84,639 in Ecuador and 40,523 in Canada (table in thousands).
Revenue moves mainly with benchmark oil prices. Q3 2026 Brent averaged $91.29 per bbl, up 34% year on year. Oil, natural gas and NGL sales rose 13% to $168.3 million.
quotes: Oil, natural gas and NGL sales for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 13% to $168.3 million, compared to the third quarter of 2025, due to increase in benchmark oil prices

business_model.claim: Quality and transportation discounts cut the South American price. They averaged $18.09 per boe in Q3 2026, against $10.76 a year earlier. The closed Colombia-Ecuador border forced costlier alternative routes for Putumayo production.
quotes: Quality and transportation discounts per boe in South America were $18.09, an increase from $10.76 in the third quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release table.
business_model.claim: Royalties are a large and price-sensitive deduction from working-interest production. Royalties were 21% of WI production in Q3 2026, against 16% a year earlier. Higher oil prices raised in-kind royalties in Ecuador.
quotes: higher in-kind royalties Ecuador driven by higher oil prices and asset sales in Canada

business_model.claim: Volumes are a second revenue driver. Net-after-royalty production fell 13% to 31,390 BOEPD from 35,962 BOEPD, because of lower Colombian output, higher Ecuador royalties and Canadian asset sales.
quotes: NAR production for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 13% to 31,390 BOEPD, compared to 35,962 BOEPD in the third quarter of 2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Canadian revenue comes from oil, natural gas and NGLs. In 2025 Canadian production was 25% oil, 24% NGLs and 51% natural gas. Q3 2026 Canadian sales were 19,066 oil, 3,403 gas and 4,304 NGL (table in thousands).
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025, 25% of NAR production in Canada was oil, compared with 21% during the two month period of 2024.

business_model.claim: The main cash operating cost is lifting cost. Q3 2026 operating expenses were $64.2 million, down 6% year on year. They were $21.32 per boe, driven by workover activity, field personnel costs and equipment maintenance.
quotes: Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 6% to $64.2 million when compared to the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to lower workover activities, reduced field personnel costs and lower equipment maintenance.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 10-Q MD&A (P4) and the income statement (F2).
growth_thesis.claim: Higher benchmark oil prices are the clearest driver of top-line growth: third-quarter sales rose to $168.3 million, up 13% on the year-earlier quarter, with Brent averaging $91.29 per bbl. Nine-month sales were 527,544 against 466,784 (table in thousands).
quotes: due to increase in benchmark oil prices

growth_thesis.basis: Differentials are stated in P4. The royalty percentages are in the P6 table. The link to growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: For price-led growth to continue, Brent must stay high and South American quality and transportation discounts must not widen further. Q3 discounts were $18.09 per boe against $10.76 a year earlier, and royalties took 21% of working-interest production against 16%.
quotes: Quality and transportation discounts per boe in South America were $18.09, an increase from $10.76 in the third quarter of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Production and royalty figures are in the P6 table. The dependence on royalties is stated in P4. The condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Ecuador is a volume-growth driver: working-interest production was 7,747 boe/d in Q3 against 3,872 boe/d a year earlier. To continue, production must keep rising faster than in-kind royalties, which took 41% of working-interest production against 33%.
quotes: higher in-kind royalties Ecuador driven by higher oil prices

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement. The reversal risk is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating cash generation improved: nine-month net cash provided by operating activities was 256,706 against 156,056, while additions to property, plant and equipment fell to 148,110 from 218,155 (table in thousands). For this to continue, the working-capital inflow that helped must not reverse.

Underlying cash earnings did not grow: Q3 funds flow from operations decreased to $31.6 million from $41.7 million, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $68.1 million against $69.0 million. Growth in cash earnings needs the sales gain to outrun higher discounts, royalties and lower volumes.
quotes: Funds flow from operations(2) decreased to $31.6 million compared to $41.7 million in the third quarter of 2025

growth_thesis.claim: Q3 volumes fell: NAR production was 31,390 BOEPD against 35,962 BOEPD, down 13%. For growth to resume, production must stabilize after the Canadian asset sales and lower Colombian output.
